title: Integral derived operations commute with finite scalar extension
statement:
Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ (inside a fixed
algebraic closure), with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, let
$f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and for
$W\in\{X,Y\}$ let
$K\mapsto K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L
=R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}_m(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m)$
be the integral scalar-extension functor [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] underlying the rational one (levelwise
modulo powers of the uniformizers), defined on derived complete objects of
$D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and carrying $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ into
$D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_L)$. For the integral derived operations
$Lf^*$, $\widehat\otimes^L$ and $R\mathcal Hom$ over $\mathcal O_E$ and over
$\mathcal O_L$ there are isomorphisms, natural in all variables,

$$
 (Lf_E^*K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong Lf_L^*(K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L),
 \qquad
 (M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong
 (M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_L}(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L),
$$
$$
 R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_E}(M,N)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L\cong
 R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_L}(M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L,N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)
$$

for $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ and $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ (the
internal Hom being derived complete because $N$ is), and for
$E\subset L\subset L'$ they are compatible with the composition isomorphisms
$(K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_{L'}\cong K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_{L'}$
and equal to the identity for $L=E$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_L$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$. The absolute-value restriction and the DVR descriptions in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give $t=uv^e$ with $u\in B^\times$ and $e\geq1$. Thus $(t^n)B=(v^{en})$. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $B/tB=B/v^eB$ is a finite set, hence a finite-dimensional vector space over $A/tA$. Choose a basis of this vector space and lift it to $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in B$. These lifts form an $A$-basis of $B$, as follows. Given $x\in B$, successively write $x_j=\sum_i a_{ij}b_i+t x_{j+1}$, starting with $x_0=x$, with $a_{ij}\in A$ chosen representatives of the residue coefficients. Then $x-\sum_i(\sum_{j<n}t^j a_{ij})b_i\in t^nB$. The inner sums converge in $A$, by completeness of $E$ in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete]; their limits belong to $A$ since its unit ball is closed. The error has norm at most $|t|^n$, hence tends to zero, proving spanning. A nonzero relation between the $b_i$ can be divided by the smallest $t$-adic valuation of its coefficients; reducing the resulting relation modulo $t$ contradicts independence of the chosen residue basis. This proves $B\cong A^d$ and also $B/t^nB\cong(A/t^nA)^d$ with one fixed basis compatible with all reductions.

proof.text: For each $W$ write $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$ as in [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Taking the inverse limit of the compatible finite-level basis isomorphisms from Step 1 gives a canonical algebra map and an isomorphism $R_W\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim} S_W$; in the chosen basis its underlying module map is $R_W^d\xrightarrow{\sim} S_W$. Indeed the subsequence $v^{en}$ has the same ordinary inverse limit as all $v^m$: extend a compatible family at indices $en$ to index $m$ by reduction from any $en\geq m$, which is independent of that choice. Finite direct sums are finite products, so taking the sheaf limit commutes with the $d$ coordinates. The map itself sends $r\otimes b$ to $rb$, so its definition is independent of the basis. In particular $S_W$ is flat over $R_W$, and tensoring with $S_W$ is an exact finite-sum functor after forgetting scalars. The coefficient reduction result [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], applied to the Noetherian DVR $A$ and its two-term free resolution $[A\xrightarrow{t^n}A]$ of $A/t^nA$, identifies $[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ with $(A/t^nA)_W$. The analogous assertion holds for $S_W$, $v^m$, and $(B/v^mB)_W$. This checks the completed, rather than constant, coefficient rings used below.

proof.text: For each $W$ and a complex $Q$ of $R_W$-modules define $C_RQ=R\lim_n(Q\otimes^L_{R_W}(A/t^nA)_W)$ using its strict tower. The completed-constant-sheaf reduction theorem [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] identifies the reduction with the two-term Koszul resolution $[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] applies and makes $C_R$ the local derived $(t)$-completion reflector.

The derived-completeness hypothesis on $K$ gives the specified Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-complete]. Step 2 shows that the canonical quotient maps $[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]\to(A/t^nA)_W$ are quasi-isomorphisms, so $t$ is injective on $R_W$ and these quotients are its quotient sheaves. Choose a K-flat representative by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and apply [lem-pur-derived-complete-koszul-reconstruction]: it identifies the strict towers in their derived category and gives an isomorphism $K\cong C_RK$ respecting the quotient projections. The strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] provides the second Roos triangle required for this comparison. For scalarRoosMap_existsUnique, construct the comparison for any additive functor directly by mappingCocone.lift: map the source cocone to the cocone of the mapped boundary, then use the product comparison square to reach the target cocone. The boundary square follows after every product projection. The two diagonal coordinate equations and the cocone degreewise biproduct identity give uniqueness; no preservation of infinite products is required for the existence of this comparison map.

proof.text: The reflector theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] says that $C_RK$ is locally derived $(t)$-complete. Restrict the isomorphism $K\cong C_RK$ from Step 4 to any slice and apply $R\mathcal Hom(R_U[1/f],-)$ for $f\in(t)(U)$: its value on $K|_U$ is isomorphic to its zero value on $(C_RK)|_U$. Thus $K$ satisfies the same local vanishing condition, and the unit criterion in the reflector theorem makes its specified unit $K\to C_RK$ invertible.

proof.text: Define $C_S$ with $v$ in the same way. Exactness of countable products follows from [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], and [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies strict derived limits with product cones, respecting strict augmentations. To apply [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality], first regard the $v$-reduction tower as modules over the constant sheaf $\underline B$ via $\underline B\to S_W$. Its countable products are exact by the same product theorem. Forgetting the $S_W$-action changes neither kernels, cokernels nor products of these module sheaves, so it preserves and detects quasi-isomorphisms and computes the same product cone. Apply the cofinality lemma with $e\geq1$ from Step 1. Its selected-coordinate and finite weighted block maps are $S_W$-linear, since every transition is $S_W$-linear. The resulting natural quasi-isomorphism therefore holds for the $S_W$-module cones as well. It identifies the full tower with the tower at indices $en$, preserves strict augmentations, and composes under further arithmetic reindexing.

proof.text: Let $T_W(Q)=Q\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ denote ordinary ambient change of rings. The construction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes it on K-flat resolutions; it is just termwise tensor since $S_W$ is finite free. The integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] is $C_S T_W(Q)$: associating the tensor products identifies each reduction with $Q\otimes^L_{R_W}(B/v^mB)_W$. Restrict to $m=en$ by Step 6. Its reduction tower is then the tensor with $S_W$ of the $t$-reduction tower of $Q$. Tensor with a finite free module commutes with termwise products: in a basis both sides are $d$ copies of the same product; the canonical map, defined without a basis, is therefore invertible. It also commutes with cones. Consequently $C_ST_W(Q)\cong T_W C_R(Q)$, naturally and $S_W$-linearly, and $T_W(Q)$ is derived complete when $Q$ is. On complete inputs integral scalar extension is therefore canonically ordinary finite free change of rings. This applies to all complete objects used below, whether or not their internal Hom is constructible. The restriction to $D^b_c$ is stipulated in the statement of the item; none of the ambient comparisons uses constructibility preservation.

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Let $F_R$ and $F_S$ be the ambient derived module pullbacks for $f$, with coefficient maps $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ and $f^{-1}S_Y\to S_X$. These maps are induced by the finite quotient maps and their limits; no assertion $f^{-1}R_Y=R_X$ is needed. The completed definitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] give $Lf_E^*K=C_R F_RK$ and $Lf_L^*T_YK=C_S F_ST_YK$. To check these equalities on towers, the quotient model from Step 2 identifies $F_RP\otimes_{R_X}(A/t^nA)_X$ with $f^{-1}(P\otimes_{R_Y}(A/t^nA)_Y)$; finite constant coefficient inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. K-flatness of ambient pullbacks is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The coefficient description $S_W=R_W\otimes_A B$ gives the ordinary comparison $T_XF_RP\cong F_S T_YP$: termwise both are $S_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}P$, using $f^{-1}(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y)=f^{-1}P\otimes_{f^{-1}R_Y}f^{-1}S_Y$ and cancelling $f^{-1}S_Y$ in the next tensor. In a basis this is the finite-sum comparison, and it is independent of that basis. Apply Step 7 to $F_RK$, and use that $C_RF_RK$ is complete by Step 5. This gives $T_X Lf_E^*K\cong C_S T_XF_RK\cong C_S F_ST_YK=Lf_L^*T_YK$, the first claimed isomorphism. The preservation of good representatives (scalarGood) uses the general coefficient-change theorem [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], which does not need finite freeness. The object and morphism formulas of integralOrdinaryScalarWitness give a degreewise isomorphism to changeOfRingsComplex. Convert IsFlatOnSite to exactness of the canonical tensorRight using [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], apply changeOfRings_isKFlat_of_flat_terms, and transport both K-flatness and termwise flatness back along that isomorphism.

For $Q=M\otimes^L_{R_W}N$, the completed tensor in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] is $C_RQ$. On K-flat representatives $P,Q'$ its $n$-th term is $(P\otimes_{R_W}Q')\otimes_{R_W}(A/t^nA)_W$, since $(P\otimes A_n)\otimes_{A_n}(Q'\otimes A_n)\cong(P\otimes Q')\otimes A_n$; these identifications respect quotient transitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the identity topos with coefficient map $R_W\to S_W$, to obtain $T_W(M\otimes^L_{R_W}N)\cong T_WM\otimes^L_{S_W}T_WN$. Step 7 and completeness of $C_RQ$ now give $T_W(M\widehat\otimes^L_{R_W}N)=T_WC_RQ\cong C_ST_WQ\cong C_S(T_WM\otimes^L_{S_W}T_WN)$. This is precisely the second displayed isomorphism. No perfectness or termwise constructibility of the resolutions has been used.

proof.text: Write $H_R(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom_{R_W}(M,N)$. It is complete if $N$ is complete. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives restriction to every slice and derived currying; on a slice its two currying isomorphisms and tensor symmetry identify $R\mathcal Hom(R_U[1/t],H_R(M,N)|_U)$ with $R\mathcal Hom(M|_U,R\mathcal Hom(R_U[1/t],N|_U))=0$. Here the last vanishing follows from the local completion criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], already identified with the reduction-tower definition in Step 4. The criterion for the generator $t$ implies the criterion for all sections in $(t)$: after inverting $at$, $t$ is invertible, and the usual localization tensor/currying identity gives the same vanishing (equivalently use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-complete-elements-ideal]). Thus Step 7 identifies scalar extension of $H_R(M,N)$ with $H_R(M,N)\otimes_{R_W}S_W$.

proof.text: To prove the third comparison, use [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and a K-injective resolution $T_WN\to J$ over $S_W$, existing by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Its restriction to $R_W$ is K-injective: for an acyclic $R_W$-complex $Z$, tensoring with the finite free $S_W$ keeps it acyclic, and the termwise tensor universal property gives $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_{R_W}(Z,\operatorname{Res}J)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_{S_W}(Z\otimes_{R_W}S_W,J)$, which is acyclic by K-injectivity. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $J$ and its $R_W$-restriction remain K-injective on every slice. Repeating the acyclic-test adjunction there computes the internal Hom complexes sectionwise, and gives $\operatorname{Res}H_S(T_WM,T_WN)\cong H_R(M,\operatorname{Res}T_WN)$. In the temporary basis $b_i$, $\operatorname{Res}T_WN=N^d$. Finite sums of a K-injective resolution of $N$ are K-injective (the Hom complex out of an acyclic input is a finite sum of acyclic complexes), and the internal Hom complex commutes with this finite sum in its second argument. Therefore the canonical map $H_R(M,N)\otimes_{R_W}S_W\to H_R(M,N\otimes_{R_W}S_W)$ is an isomorphism: in the basis it is the identity on $d$ copies of $H_R(M,N)$. Its sectionwise formula is $h\otimes s\mapsto(m\mapsto h(m)\otimes s)$, so it is $S_W$-linear and independent of the basis. Combining with the preceding adjunction and Step 7 proves the third isomorphism for arbitrary complete $M,N$, in particular the stated constructible ones. This proves the derived scalar adjunction here rather than invoking the finite-Tor-only comparison of another node.

proof.text: All comparisons above come from strict-tower maps, tensor universal maps, and evaluation, so they are natural in their inputs. For $E\subset L\subset L'$, write $S'_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L',W}$. Repeat Steps 1--2 and the scalar-extension construction of Step 7 for both inclusions. The integral composition map is induced by $(P\otimes_{R_W}S_W)\otimes_{S_W}S'_W\to P\otimes_{R_W}S'_W$, $(p\otimes s)\otimes s'\mapsto p\otimes ss'$, and the completion comparisons. The two pullback routes both send a local tensor $a\otimes(p\otimes s)\otimes s'$ to $a\otimes p\otimes ss'$. The two tensor routes both send $(m\otimes s)\otimes(n\otimes t')\otimes u'$ to $(m\otimes n)\otimes st'u'$ after the appropriate ring embeddings. For internal Hom, uncurry the two routes using the termwise adjunction in Step 11: both send $(h\otimes s\otimes s',m\otimes t')$ to $h(m)\otimes ss't'$ in $N\otimes S'_W$. These equalities hold on sheaf tensors because local pure tensors generate, and commute with differentials, quotients, transition maps, products and cones. Thus they remain equal in the derived categories and after completion. The generator formulas define the maps; the bases were used only to prove they are invertible. For $L=E$, scalar extension is $C_R$ and its canonical comparison with the identity on complete objects is the completion unit of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]; under this identification all three formulas are identities. This proves the identity clause in its usual categorical sense (the originally displayed functor is a product-cone construction, not literally the identity on representatives). No rational-composition statement is used to infer integral coherence. In Lean, scalarHomOrdinary_naturality is proved for arbitrary coefficient closed structures and any functor with a tensor comparison: uncurry both sides, use the inverse tensor-comparison naturality squares, and apply evaluation naturality in both variables. Injectivity of the transpose equivalence then proves the desired equation without any finite-free or completeness argument.

lean.statement: theorem scalarOperationsOrdinary_tower (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra ℚ_[l] F] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] F] (j : L →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] F) {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (W : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}) : (∀ K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E Y), (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l L F j X).map ((scalarPullbackOrdinary l E L ι f).hom.app K) ≫ (scalarPullbackOrdinary l L F j f).hom.app ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι Y).obj K) ≫ (integralDerivedPullback l F f).map ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι Y F j).hom.app K) = (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι X F j).hom.app ((integralDerivedPullback l E f).obj K) ≫ (scalarPullbackOrdinary l E F (j.comp ι) f).hom.app K) ∧ (∀ M N : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E W), (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l L F j W).map ((scalarTensorOrdinary l E L ι W).hom.app (M, N)) ≫ (scalarTensorOrdinary l L F j W).hom.app ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι W).obj M, (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι W).obj N) ≫ (integralCompletedTensor l F W).map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι W F j).hom.app M) ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι W F j).hom.app N)) = (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι W F j).hom.app ((integralCompletedTensor l E W).obj (M, N)) ≫ (scalarTensorOrdinary l E F (j.comp ι) W).hom.app (M, N)) ∧ (∀ M N : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E W), (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l L F j W).map (scalarHomOrdinary l E L ι W M N) ≫ scalarHomOrdinary l L F j W ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι W).obj M) ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar l E L ι W).obj N) ≫ (integralDerivedInternalHom l F W).map (CategoryTheory.Prod.mkHom (((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι W F j).inv.app M).op) ((integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι W F j).hom.app N)) = (integralOrdinaryDerivedScalarComp l E L ι W F j).hom.app ((integralDerivedInternalHom l E W).obj (op M, N)) ≫ scalarHomOrdinary l E F (j.comp ι) W M N)
lean.note: Interface repair under brief §1(B): the previous Comparisons proposition supplied natural/tower/unit isomorphisms without fixing pullback/tensor/Hom components on representatives, and used literal coefficient subfields in the scheme universe. This supplementary module imports the original theorem unchanged and adds uniquely normalized strict level/tower/Roos maps, their derived comparisons and ordinary tower/unit identities, completion comparisons, and evaluation-transposed Hom. Arbitrary small finite coefficient models support algebraic closures in an independent universe. Definitions use real maps or uniquely characterized localization data, never an arbitrary existential comparison.
